entities.summary: José Luis Cuevas was a Mexican artist, he often worked as a painter, writer, draftsman, engraver, illustrator, and printmaker. Cuevas was one of the first to challenge the then dominant Mexican muralism movement as a prominent member of the Generación de la Ruptura. He was a mostly self-taught artist, whose styles and influences are moored to the darker side of life, often depicting distorted figures and the debasement of humanity. He had remained a controversial figure throughout his career, not only for his often shocking images, but also for his opposition to writers and artists who he feels participate in corruption or create only for money.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent member of the Generación de la Ruptura, Cuevas challenged traditional Mexican muralism with his dark and distorted depictions of humanity, influencing the development of Mexican art and literature in the mid-20th century.
